summary: Shared ephemeral idempotency key in client-side batching causes duplicated downstream side-effects under burst streaming load
description:
Issue summary:
Customer observed duplicated downstream database writes when sending high-volume streaming requests that include function/tool calls. The customer batches user events client-side into a single streaming session and (for performance) attaches a short-lived, shared idempotency token per-batch. Under burst load and when the SDK automatically retries transient connection errors, the same ephemeral token is reused across replays resulting in duplicate tool invocations recorded by the customer's downstream webhook consumer.

Impact:
Multiple customers at NimbusB2B experienced duplicate order-creation side-effects (database rows duplicated) for ~0.2% of streamed requests during peak load (approx 10k requests/min sustained over 3 minutes). No token leakage across different tenants reported, but duplicates are causing accounting/card-charge reconciliation issues.

Environment:
- Customer: dedicated account on prod:us-east
- SDK: python-sdk v1.3.2 (they report using the streaming client with custom batching wrapper)
- Server-side: Redwood hosted inference (running open-redwood/v0.9-chat-small)

Observed behavior:
- Client opens long-lived streaming session and sends 5 event messages per user in a single batch with a per-batch ephemeral idempotency key (TTL ~30s).
- Intermittent network hiccup causes SDK to reconnect and perform an automatic retry of in-flight messages. Because the ephemeral token was generated once for the whole batch scope, retried messages reuse the same token and downstream tool calls are executed again.

Expected behavior:
- SDK retries should not cause duplicate tool invocation when application-level side-effects are present. Either retries should be scoped per-request or the SDK should surface retries such that callers can provide per-operation dedupe tokens.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Use python-sdk v1.3.2 streaming client with a custom client-side batcher that attaches a single ephemeral idempotency token to the whole batch.
2) Configure a downstream webhook that performs a write on function/tool invocation (e.g., create_order endpoint).
3) Simulate intermittent network failure causing reconnects (tcp reset or short infra blip) while a batch is in-flight.
4) Observe duplicate webhook POSTs and duplicate DB rows for some batches.

Logs:
- Customer provided sampled SDK client logs (attached in ticket). Excerpts show reconnect + automatic retransmit with identical batch header X-Idempotency: ephem-abc123.
- Server-side traces (linked): trace id rwd-20260310-8f7a (shows two successful funcall deliveries for the same request identifiers).

Workaround used by customer:
- NimbusB2B temporarily changed their batcher to emit per-message idempotency tokens rather than per-batch tokens; duplication rate dropped to <0.01% but added extra token generation overhead and complexity.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Create a python streaming client with a batcher that attaches a single ephemeral idempotency token for N messages.
2) Start a downstream webhook that records function/tool side-effects.
3) Inject a short network interruption during batch transmit (e.g., iptables drop or simulate client reconnect).
4) Observe duplicate POSTs and DB writes when SDK auto-retries the in-flight batch with the same token.
investigation_notes:
- Initial hypothesis: idempotency token scope (per-batch vs per-message) combined with SDK-level automatic retransmission leads to duplicate funcalls.
- Verified server traces: two deliveries with identical idempotency header value and same session id; both accepted by router and routed to serving runtime.
- SDK behavior: python-sdk v1.3.2 implements an optimistic in-flight message retransmit on connection resume; it re-sends headers as originally set.
- Edge case: token TTL shorter than retry window could also cause token reuse if client reuses cached token value.
- Repro script: created internal load harness that reproduces duplicate at ~5k rps when batching factor >=4 and artificial 200-500ms reconnect introduced.
- Related to existing tickets: SUP-314159 (batching normalization) and INT-5412 (go-proxy retransmit logic) — cross-referenced for routing logic similarities.
comments: 2026-03-10 09:12 - Maya Rodriguez: Customer reported via support intake. Provided initial example logs and sample client code. Marked as P1 due to billing/duplication impact.

2026-03-10 10:04 - Liam Chen (SRE): Acknowledged. Asked the customer for reproducible test case and permission to run internal replay harness against their tenant in a limited window. Added components: sdk-python, streaming.

2026-03-10 13:30 - NimbusB2B-Eng (customer): Shared a minimal repro and confirmed they see duplicate create_order requests in their DB but only during bursts. Offered to schedule a short test window 2026-03-11 02:00 UTC.

2026-03-11 02:15 - Liam Chen: Ran controlled repro in collaboration with customer; confirmed duplicates with per-batch token, eliminated when per-message tokens used. Captured server traces and packet captures (links added to ticket).

2026-03-11 15:40 - SRE Lead (Priya Kapoor): Noted design tradeoff: SDK automatic retransmit is intended to improve reliability but currently preserves original headers. Propose SDK change to: (A) surface retry notifications to caller, and/or (B) support an optional per-message dedupe callback so callers can supply unique tokens per message.

2026-03-12 09:05 - Engineering (runtime team): Confirmed server currently treats idempotency header as authoritative and will accept any valid token as unique invocation key — server-side dedupe requires canonicalization and persistent dedupe store which has cost/latency tradeoffs. Suggested short-term mitigation by implementing lightweight server-side best-effort dedupe for ephemeral tokens with TTL=60s for dedicated customers with high-traffic flags.

2026-03-12 12:00 - Liam Chen: Documented short-term workaround and next steps. Assigned follow-up engineering task INT-5580 to add telemetry and config flag to enable best-effort dedupe for scoped tokens in Dedicated accounts. Requested product review for longer-term SDK ergonomics changes.
resolution: Workaround: Customer moved to per-message idempotency tokens (recommended) which reduced duplicates to acceptable levels. Short-term mitigation: engineering to enable a best-effort server-side dedupe toggle for impacted dedicated customers (INT-5580). Long-term: SDK change for retry visibility + optional per-message dedupe helpers planned (tracked in SDK RFC and linked PRs).
follow_up_actions: INT-5580: add best-effort dedupe toggle for dedicated accounts
Confluence: update streaming idempotency guidance page with recommended per-message token pattern
